name: Fatou Reinholt-Chandra
subcategory: Spire portrait painter / physical oil on canvas
creator: Fatou Reinholt-Chandra
description: The only working oil-on-canvas portraitist with a consistent Tier 5 clientele, Reinholt-Chandra charges sums that would constitute a Tier 2 family's decade of income for a single commission — and has a waiting list extending seven years. Her portraits are technically flawless and psychologically devastating, a combination that has made her both indispensable and quietly feared among Spire elites who commission her. She is known to spend months with her subjects before beginning to paint, and several clients have attempted to withdraw commissions after preliminary sittings, apparently unsettled by what she has observed.
cultural_impact: Reinholt-Chandra's portraits have become the definitive status objects of Meridian 88's Tier 5 — more significant than any corporate title or chrome augmentation — while simultaneously functioning as the most penetrating psychological record of Spire culture ever assembled, since every subject believes their portrait flatters them.
controversy: Three of her subjects have died under suspicious circumstances within a year of their portraits' completion; this is almost certainly coincidence but has generated persistent dark mythology. One former client is rumored to have paid significant sums to have their portrait destroyed; it is rumored to still exist.
story_hooks: A Tier 5 client has died and their estate is contesting the will; the portrait Reinholt-Chandra painted — which the deceased never allowed anyone to see — has been named as a piece of evidence in the proceedings.
Reinholt-Chandra has quietly accepted a commission from someone claiming Tier 5 status whose identity cannot be verified through any corporate registry.
She has approached a Shelf-born individual with no Quanta to offer, saying she wants to paint them and will accept no payment — and will not explain why.
